arguments.summary: Latest normalized SEC facts quantify balance-sheet funding but not a comparable interest-expense, customer-financing, or demand-elasticity measure for all four issuers. The clearest filing-supported direct financing sensitivity is NVIDIA: its July 2026 10-Q reports $1.0bn short-term and $32.366bn long-term debt, alongside $22.443bn cash; therefore debt financing—not merely equity-duration valuation—can be a conditional transmission channel. Meta reports $83.664bn long-term debt and $15.462bn cash at June 2026; this identifies a potential financing channel but does not quantify coupon, maturity, floating-rate share, or interest expense. ANET and MU supplied normalized facts omit long-term-debt fields and interest expense, so their direct-rate sensitivity cannot be ranked. No retrieved filing evidence quantifies customer financing or an issuer-specific macro-demand elasticity; use a conditional customer-capex/advertising-demand channel only.

claims.text: NVIDIA's latest 10-Q (quarter ended July 26, 2026) reports $1.0bn short-term debt, $32.366bn long-term debt, and $22.443bn cash and cash equivalents; its six-month cash-flow statement reports $24.896bn of net debt-issuance proceeds. The filing excerpt does not provide interest expense, coupon, maturity, or fixed/floating-rate detail in the retrieved portion.

NVIDIA's disclosed debt makes refinancing or incremental borrowing costs a plausible direct monetary-policy channel, but its 21/63-session earnings sensitivity cannot be quantified without debt terms, maturities, rate mix, and interest expense; the large reported cash balance may partly offset gross-debt sensitivity but does not establish net interest exposure.

Meta's latest normalized 10-Q facts, for June 30, 2026, report $83.664bn long-term debt and $15.462bn cash and cash equivalents. The supplied normalized facts do not include interest expense or debt-rate/maturity detail.

Meta's reported long-term debt identifies a potential direct financing channel, but the available filing evidence cannot establish whether policy changes materially alter its 21/63-session interest cost. Separately, advertising demand could be cyclical, but no retrieved filing excerpt quantifies macro sensitivity or customer financing.

ANET's June 30, 2026 normalized 10-Q facts report $2.902bn cash and cash equivalents, while MU's May 28, 2026 normalized 10-Q facts report $24.995bn cash. Neither supplied normalized record reports long-term debt or interest expense.

If tighter financial conditions reduce enterprise/cloud capital budgets, ANET, MU, and NVDA could face demand effects; if broader growth weakens, Meta advertising demand could be affected. This is a scenario only: no retrieved filing evidence quantifies customer financing, customer concentration, order cancellation sensitivity, or macro-demand elasticity for these issuers.

gaps.description: No comparable latest-filing interest expense, debt coupon/maturity schedule, fixed/floating-rate mix, hedging, or refinancing calendar was retrieved for any issuer; direct 21/63-session rate sensitivity cannot be quantified or ranked.
No retrieved filing excerpt quantifies customer financing, customer credit dependence, or macro-demand elasticity for ANET, MU, META, or NVDA.

assumptions: Gross debt and cash are balance-sheet indicators, not measures of interest expense or net interest-rate sensitivity.
Demand transmission is conditional on customer budget and advertising-cycle responses, which are unmeasured here.
arguments.counter_thesis: Near-term operating demand, product cycles, and valuation discount-rate changes may dominate any direct interest-cost effect; the available filing extracts do not demonstrate that financing costs materially alter earnings over 21/63 sessions.

review_conditions.description: Review the next issuer filings for interest expense, debt maturity/rate mix, customer-financing arrangements, and quantified demand or customer-concentration disclosures before assigning relative monetary-policy sensitivity.

question_effects.reason: Filings identify gross-debt financing channels for NVDA and META, but do not quantify interest-cost sensitivity, customer financing, or demand elasticity; generic macro transmission should remain conditional rather than issuer-ranked.

role_coverage.reason: Reviewed available latest issuer filing evidence and normalized facts for direct funding and demand-transmission disclosures; material quantification gaps remain explicit.

shared_exposures.mechanism: Conditional monetary-policy transmission through financing costs and customer budget/advertising-cycle demand.
shared_exposures.qualification: NVDA and Meta gross debt are reported; issuer-specific interest-rate sensitivity and demand elasticities are not. ANET and MU direct funding exposure is not established from supplied normalized facts.
